result.title: Sharp First-Hit Identification from Finite Depth Samples
result.comment: 36 pages, 9 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
result.summary: Which depths in a new camera view are determined by finitely many source-depth measurements? Pointwise uncertainty bounds do not answer this question: unobserved geometry between samples can change which surface is encountered first. We study a bounded Lipschitz class of continuous source inverse-depth fields with interval observations and known camera pose. Building on classical Lipschitz envelopes, we characterize the exact set of attainable first-hit depths and construct a globally admissible scene for every value in that set. The set can be disconnected. We also give a necessary and sufficient test for several proposed depths to be first hits of one shared scene. An epipolar reduction uses scalar cone inequalities without enumerating surfaces. In a rectified model with source spacing $h$, interval half-width $\varepsilon$, baseline $b$, and slope bound $L$, we prove a sharp worst-case inverse-depth diameter of $\max\{Lh+2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon/(1-bL)\}$ when $bL<1$, subject to sufficient depth and domain range for attainment. Exact samples still give the sharp bound $Lh$ at $bL=1$, while above this threshold ambiguity need not vanish as sampling becomes arbitrarily dense. Any positive measurement uncertainty can destroy uniform stability at the critical threshold. We provide constructive examples, an exact rational validation oracle, and a frozen ten-scene evaluation using reference, stereo, and learned-depth observations. The experiments separate solver correctness under the scene assumptions from failure of those assumptions: fixed learned-depth bands often yield narrow but incorrect sets. The results identify what a specified scene class permits; they do not infer a continuum regularity or physical-scene guarantee from sampled predictions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究有限深度采样下新视角首达深度的可识别性：以有界 Lipschitz 逆深度场刻画可达首达深度集合，给出尖锐的最坏情形逆深度直径界、多深度共场景可行性检验与有理数验证器，并在含立体与学习深度的场景上做固定评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 它形式化地刻画有限视觉观测能约束多少首达几何，并指出超过临界基线斜率后加密采样也无法消除歧义，可能为 LVR 中「视觉证据是否充分、何时停止获取」提供参照，且提示学习深度带可能给出窄但错误的可达集合，可供核查。
